steps.note: Seeded, then cooled slowly, about 3 °C/h from 60 to 30 °C and about 1.5 °C/h to 15 °C, so the lactose crystallises out in crystals over 0.2 mm that separate best.
The crystals go through a decanter, then a sieve centrifuge, and are washed; two decanter centrifuges in series leave a lactose cake under 9 % moisture, about 99 % dry solids.

lactose.text: Lactose is much less soluble when cold, so a concentrated permeate is cooled slowly and the lactose crystallises out (as alpha-lactose monohydrate). The crystals are spun off, washed and dried; the mother liquor keeps the minerals and the rest of the sugar.
